stories.headline: Nvidia Pays $6 Billion for Poolside's Model Factory and 109 of the People Who Built It
stories.key_takeaway: Nvidia is paying $6 billion for a non-exclusive license to Poolside's Model Factory and hiring 109 of the engineers behind it - the third such structure in a year, bringing Nvidia's licensing spend to roughly $27 billion without a single merger filing.

pull_quote.text: Less than 70 people built this model.

stories.article_excerpt: Nvidia has agreed to pay Poolside $6 billion for a non-exclusive license to the software the startup used to build its AI models, hire 109 of its employees, and invest a further $1 billion in whatever is left.

stories.headline: Broadcom Is Borrowing Up to $100 Billion to Buy Its Own Customers Their Chips
stories.key_takeaway: Broadcom is seeking more than $60 billion in senior secured debt - potentially $100 billion with a junior tranche - routed through special-purpose vehicles that lease AI racks to Anthropic and others, leaving Broadcom guaranteeing lease payments on the chips it sells.

pull_quote.text: We are at a historic inflection point where the demand for AI compute is fundamentally reshaping the global economic landscape.

stories.article_excerpt: Broadcom is in the market for one of the largest corporate borrowings ever assembled, and almost none of it will show up on its balance sheet.

stories.headline: Anthropic's Benchmark for Its IPO Is No Longer OpenAI. It Is SpaceX's $86 Billion Record.
stories.key_takeaway: Anthropic expects an IPO matching or beating SpaceX's record $86.2 billion raise, with shareholders floating a $2 trillion price on a company that posted $11.5 billion in quarterly revenue and a $42 billion annual loss.

pull_quote.text: The most accurate criticism of AI companies, including Anthropic, is that we haven't yet delivered on our big promises to benefit the world.

stories.article_excerpt: The benchmark Anthropic is now measuring itself against is not OpenAI. It is SpaceX.

stories.headline: Nvidia Is Talking to the Korean Startup That Promised to Stand Up to Nvidia
stories.key_takeaway: Jensen Huang met Rebellions CEO Sunghyun Park in Santa Clara to discuss a partnership, investment or acquisition - the fourth time in a year Nvidia has moved on a rival inference architecture, and the first where a foreign government is a direct shareholder.

pull_quote.text: Rebellions' goal and journey is to confidently stand up to the giant called Nvidia and advance into the global market within the next two to three years.

stories.article_excerpt: Jensen Huang spent part of this week in a conference room at Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters with a man whose stated ambition is to break Nvidia's monopoly.

stories.headline: The ECB Says an AI Correction Is Coming Whether or Not the Bubble Is Real
stories.key_takeaway: Five ECB economists argue a correction in US equity valuations is likely under both the rational and the behavioural reading of the AI rally, and put euro-area household exposure to US tech - held largely unknowingly through index funds - at around 440 billion euros.

pull_quote.text: This is why a Mag7 correction is a question of financial stability for the euro area, rather than just a private one.
pull_quote.attribution: Andersson, Breckenfelder, Corradin, Nikolov and Viola

data_points.label: Euro-area household exposure to US tech
Mag7 share of S&P 500 market cap

stories.article_excerpt: Central banks rarely tell you a crash is coming. They hedge, they qualify, they publish charts and let you draw the line yourself.

stories.headline: Nevada Told Tesla It Could Run Ten Robotaxis. Twenty-Four Days Later It Said Five Thousand.
stories.key_takeaway: The Nevada Transportation Authority unanimously cleared Tesla for up to 5,000 paid robotaxis in Clark County - 500 times the cap it granted on July 27 - even as Tesla's own Cybercab chief engineer said 2,500 would be a good year.

pull_quote.text: The 5,000 has always been a ceiling for us.

data_points.label: Cap in the July 27 interim permit
Cap each for Waymo and Aviari

stories.article_excerpt: Twenty-four days ago, Nevada regulators told Tesla it could operate exactly ten driverless cars on the Las Vegas Strip. On Thursday, the same agency raised that ceiling by a factor of 500.

stories.headline: ChatGPT Can Now Read Your iMessages. Full Disk Access Is the Price of Entry.
stories.key_takeaway: OpenAI's new macOS plugin lets ChatGPT read, search and send iMessage, SMS and RCS threads locally through AppleScript and Accessibility - confined for now to ChatGPT Work and Codex, with per-send approval as the only real defence against prompt injection.

pull_quote.text: Giving an agent a very broad instruction such as 'review my emails and take whatever action is needed' can make it easier for hidden malicious content to mislead the model, even though it is designed to check with you before taking sensitive actions.

data_points.label: Message types read: iMessage, SMS, RCS

stories.article_excerpt: OpenAI's assistant has been handed a seat inside the most private app on the Mac. As of August 20, a mainstream chatbot can be pointed at a decade of your text messages and told to act on them.

stories.headline: Gemma Passes a Billion Downloads, and Qwen Still Has Twice as Many Descendants
stories.key_takeaway: Google says Gemma has passed a billion cumulative downloads and 100,000 community variants, but Hugging Face data puts Qwen derivatives at 151,448 against Google's 82,506 - Gemma is the strongest US open family and still a distant second.

pull_quote.text: What matters far more than the download count is what the community is building with them.
pull_quote.role: Vice president and product director, Google DeepMind

stories.article_excerpt: Google spent the week talking about Gemini. The more consequential number came from the models it gives away.

stories.headline: Binance Let AI Agents Trade for 300 Million Users and Set No Limit on What They Can Lose
stories.key_takeaway: Binance's Agent OS lets AI agents place live trades from dedicated subaccounts with withdrawals blocked, but the exchange sets no drawdown cap, no maximum position and no circuit breaker - and says it cannot see the reasoning behind any order.

pull_quote.text: Instead of total freedom, we put the power in users' hands to give them the granular access control of what they can do through the agent.

data_points.label: Daily cap on Agentic Wallet swaps

stories.article_excerpt: Binance spent Thursday doing something no exchange of its size had done before: it handed AI agents the keys to a live trading account and declined to say how much they were allowed to lose.

stories.headline: Apple Music Will Label AI Songs, but Only the Ones Distributors Admit To
stories.key_takeaway: Apple will turn its voluntary AI Transparency Tags into a required, consumer-visible 'Made With AI' badge later this year - but the badge depends on distributors self-reporting, while Deezer, which detects AI tracks itself, now sees 90,000 synthetic uploads a day.

pull_quote.text: We have reached a pivotal moment, but we have the technology to keep track of the development, and an ambition to do what's right.

data_points.label: Fully AI tracks uploaded daily to Deezer
Share of new daily uploads, June 2026
Listeners who want AI music labelled

stories.article_excerpt: Apple has spent five months letting the music industry decide, quietly, whether to admit a song was made by a machine. That grace period is ending.

stories.headline: MIT Says Train on Enough Art and No Single Artist Can Claim the Output
stories.key_takeaway: An MIT CSAIL team publishing in Nature Communications shows that as diffusion training sets grow, the influence of any single image decays on an inverse power law - meaning outputs from large-scale scrapes may be legally unattributable to any one work.

pull_quote.text: If you take away a piece of data and the output of the model doesn't change, then that piece of data didn't affect the output.
pull_quote.role: Lead author, former MIT CSAIL researcher

stories.article_excerpt: The image atop MIT's press release is a portrait nobody painted. Beside it sit more than 200 near-identical versions of the same face.

stories.headline: Samsung Put a 1.2-Million-Parameter Health Model on a Watch. It Answers in Under a Millisecond.
stories.key_takeaway: Samsung Research America's HiMAE runs health inference on a smartwatch CPU in under a millisecond from about 1.2 million parameters, while its companion xMAE uses discarded ECG scaffolding to make cheap optical pulse data behave like a clinical signal.

pull_quote.text: in wearable health AI, the pretraining objective and physiological inductive bias can be as important as model scale.
pull_quote.attribution: Hao Zhou and Sharanya Arcot Desai
pull_quote.role: Researchers, Digital Health Team, Samsung Research America

stories.article_excerpt: Foundation models are supposed to be enormous. The one Samsung Research America just put on a smartwatch has about 1.2 million parameters.
